title: Fanout affinity drift causing multi-region SLO miss — investigation & action plan
creator: Priya Nair
impact_summary: 2026-03-09 17:22 - 2026-03-09 19:10 UTC: Production traffic experienced uneven regional fanout that caused sustained 99th percentile end-to-end latency SLO breaches for ~1.5 hours. Affected hosted API customers in EU and APAC regions experienced request timeouts and elevated tail latency; total error budget burn estimated at ~4.3% of monthly budget for the affected orgs. Root visible symptoms: elevated queue length on EU secondary routing pools, repeated circuit breaker trips in ap-east-1 replicas, and cold KV-cache miss rates rising from baseline 2% to 28% on warmup followed by cascading priority eviction.
metrics: Max p99 latency (global): 1.8s (SLO target 0.5s for interactive routes)
Error rate spike: 0.9% -> 5.8% for chat/generation endpoints during window
Queue depth on EU-secondary routing pool: sustained 3500 requests (baseline 200)
KV cache miss rate in ap-east-1 hot path: 28% (baseline 2%)
Circuit breaker open count: 42 distinct hosts tripped across regions
Estimated customer error-budget burn: 4.3% for impacted tenants
timeline: 2026-03-09 17:22 UTC: Automated SLO alert fired for global p99 latency; on-call page triggered.
2026-03-09 17:27 UTC: Initial operator investigation shows disproportionate traffic routed to eu-west-1 secondary pool; control-plane routing snapshot was lagging.
2026-03-09 17:35 UTC: Circuit breakers in ap-east-1 begin tripping due to bursty cold-KV misses; traffic refanouts observed.
2026-03-09 17:42 UTC: Quick mitigation — scaled up eu-west-1 dedicated pool capacity and temporarily disabled a new affinity-reshuffle feature rolled out earlier that day.
2026-03-09 18:05 UTC: Error rates and p99 improved but oscillation persisted due to mismatch between routing affinity TTLs and circuit hysteresis windows.
2026-03-09 18:50 UTC: Gradual stabilization observed after KV-cache pre-warm tasks and rolling restart of routing agents; alerts suppressed at 19:10 UTC after sustained recovery.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Post-incident data collection and initial RCA meeting held with runtime, routing, and control-plane teams.
root_cause: Three contributory factors aligned: 1) A control-plane change earlier that day reduced the affinity update batching window from 30s to 5s to improve rebalancing; an edge case in the new batching code caused periods where affinity tables were stale for up to 90s under high write contention. 2) A simultaneous canary of a 'priority weight' change increased low-priority route burstiness, which amplified cold-KV cache churn in secondary region replicas. 3) Circuit-breaker hysteresis thresholds were narrowly tuned, so temporary latency spikes triggered opens that caused fanout oscillation and re-routing waves. The combined effect was that traffic concentrated on suboptimal secondary pools, KV caches suffered cold misses, hosts tripped, and the system entered a self-reinforcing feedback loop.
mitigations_deployed: Rollback affinity batching change to previous stable version (rolled at 17:52 UTC)
Hotfix: increased circuit-breaker hysteresis window from 30s to 90s for cross-region routing (deployed at 18:00 UTC)
Scale up temporary capacity in eu-west-1 pool by +40% to absorb backpressure (manual scale at 17:45 UTC)
KV-cache pre-warm job run for impacted model shards in ap-east-1 and eu-west-1 (kicked at 17:55 UTC)
long_term_actions: (A1) Routing affinity engine: add deterministic reconciliation and instrumentation for stale-table windows; owner: Liam O'Connor; due: 2026-03-30
(A2) Affinity rollout guard: implement preflight checks that simulate high write contention at canary scale; owner: Sofia Martinez; due: 2026-04-06
(A3) Circuit breaker tuning: introduce adaptive hysteresis tied to KV-cache miss signal to avoid blind opens; owner: Ethan Zhao; due: 2026-04-13
(A4) Priority-weight rollout policy: require synthetic workload verification and cost-of-warmup estimation before global rollouts; owner: Priya Nair; due: 2026-04-20
(A5) Observability: add per-routing-pool 'fanout-entropy' metric and alert when >2x baseline; owner: Devops Team (rotation) - lead: Anika Patel; due: 2026-03-24
(A6) Runbook: update multi-region failover playbook to include explicit KV-cache warmup step and a safe-scaling checklist; owner: Reliability Docs; due: 2026-03-18
action_items: Ethan Zhao: Implement adaptive circuit hysteresis prototype and land a dashboard for hysteresis health - due 2026-04-13
Liam O'Connor: Add reconciliation trace logs and a reconciliation SLA metric for affinity tables - due 2026-03-30
Sofia Martinez: Implement affine-batching preflight canary harness and block rollout without synthetic pass - due 2026-04-06
Priya Nair: Create a regression test that reproduces high write contention and validates no stale windows beyond 30s - due 2026-03-20
Anika Patel: Add 'fanout-entropy' and 'kv-warmup-complete' to the Console per-route dashboard and set initial thresholds - due 2026-03-24
Reliability Docs: Update runbook and circulate to SRE rotation for tabletop on 2026-03-22 - due 2026-03-18
postmortem_notes: This incident is notable because it was caused by an interaction between two low-risk changes that individually would have been safe: affinity batching change (intended to reduce churn) and a priority-weight tweak (intended to improve fairness). The missing guardrail was a lack of cross-feature integration tests and insufficient telemetry coupling between affinity staleness and circuit-breaker health. We should treat cross-cutting rollout interactions as first-class in our preflight policies.
review_comments: PM (Sanjay Rao): Good identification of cross-feature risk. Recommend adding a policy to require cross-team review for any affinity or routing changes.
Design (Maya Lopez): Observability panels are useful; suggest a compact 'triage' view for on-call to see fanout-entropy + kv-miss + cb-open in one glance.
SRE (Jordan Kim): Circuit hysteresis increase helped but is a band-aid; adaptive hysteresis is required to prevent similar future oscillations.
conclusion: Primary corrective actions are committed: rollback of the risky affinity batching change, short-term circuit hysteresis increase, and a concrete set of long-term mitigations with owners and dates. We will run a tabletop exercise on 2026-03-22 to validate the updated runbook and deployment gates. This ticket will track follow-up action completion and be closed when all A* items are marked done.
